questions.text: What is the register map of the test shell (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: 32-bit registers at 0x00 SHELL_ID, 0x04 TICK, 0x08 STATUS, 0x0C REPLY_LEN, 0x10 REPLY_WORD_IDX, 0x14 REPLY_WORD, 0x18 TELE_LEN, 0x1C TELE_WORD_IDX, 0x20 TELE_WORD, 0x24 TELE_TAKE, 0x28 PACKET_BYTE, as in registers.map
questions.reason: The request names shell registers but gives no offsets, so the map is a proposal.
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)
questions.evidence: IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag

questions.text: How is the last flag of a payload byte given through the shell?
questions.answer: Through the IN register at offset 0 (WO). Bits [7:0] carry the packet byte and bit 8 is the end flag. The spec does not use the name PACKET_BYTE, so the proposed default is correct on the bit but should refer to IN.

questions.default: No, only successfully executed commands (including status, start, stop).
questions.reason: The count is of commands carried out.
questions.answer: No, only successfully executed commands (including status, start, stop).

questions.text: When does the first telemetry frame fall due after a start?
questions.default: After period ticks counted from the start command.
questions.reason: The request says start restarts the count.
questions.answer: Confirmed: the first frame falls due at the period-th tick counted from the start command. The spec says TLM_START restarts the count and that a frame falls due every period ticks. A period of 0 keeps the current period, and a period below 4 is raised to 4.
questions.evidence: Pacer: TLM_START restarts the count (period 0 keeps, below 4 raised to 4); a frame falls due every period ticks; one held frame; overruns dropped; STOP forgets the held frame; TAKE releases it.
